stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In August 1941, before the United States entered World War II, President Franklin Roosevelt and Prime Minister Winston Churchill met aboard ships off Newfoundland and issued a joint statement of war aims known as the Atlantic Charter. The statement said neither nation sought new territory, that all peoples had the right to choose their own form of government, that trade should be open and free, and that all nations should be free from fear and want. It also called for disarming aggressor nations and building a wider system of general security after the war.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary summary of the Atlantic Charter, August 1941, as described in Barron's Chapter 9 and Princeton Chapter 11.

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded paraphrases, tables, and photographs (see source_note)
stem: According to the Atlantic Charter, what right did all peoples hold?

options.text: The right to trade only with the United States
options.misconception: The Charter called for open trade among all nations, not trade with one nation alone.

options.text: The right to choose their own form of government
The right to keep the territory they had conquered
options.misconception: The Charter said neither nation sought new territory from the war.

options.text: The right to build armies without any limits
options.misconception: The Charter called for disarming aggressor nations, not for unlimited armies.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the Charter called for open trade among all nations, not trade with one nation alone.
rationales.B: The Charter promised self-determination, so peoples could choose their own governments instead of having rule imposed on them.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the Charter said neither nation sought new territory.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the Charter called for disarming aggressor nations, not for unlimited armies.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says the Charter gave all peoples the right to choose their own form of government.
2. It also said neither nation sought new territory from the war.
3. Background: Roosevelt and Churchill issued the Charter in August 1941, before the United States entered the war.
4. Self-determination meant peoples would not be handed from one ruler to another as spoils.
Remember: self-determination means a people picks its own government.
